text:
Utah did not just win this one, it buried Chicago before the second period was half over. Dylan Guenther's power-play snap shot at 16:41 of the first opened the scoring, and Michael Carcone made it 2-0 just 40 seconds later. By 15:28 of the second, Guenther had tipped in a second power-play goal and it was 5-0. The score matched the play: Utah's expected goals were 3.89 to Chicago's 1.69, and in simulated replays of every shot the Mammoth win 84 percent of the time.

The gap was widest in the middle of the game. Utah generated 1.96 expected goals in the second period against 0.43 for Chicago, and finished with 65 shot attempts to 42. Arvid Soderblom faced 32 shots and allowed 6 on 3.89 expected, so he was about two goals worse than an average goalie on those chances. Utah also won 39 of 54 faceoffs, hit Chicago 42 times to 12, and went 2 for 3 on the power play while Chicago went 0 for 3. Clayton Keller picked up two assists and Anders Lee, Nick Schmaltz and Daniil But added even-strength goals.

At the other end, Karel Vejmelka stopped all 15 shots, which was exactly what the chances called for (1.69 expected goals against, so he was a touch better than average). Chicago's best stretch came in the third, when it outchanced Utah 0.76 to 0.38, but with the game long decided, that was never going to matter. But added the last goal at 12:50 off a tip, and Utah closed out a shutout that its play had earned.
